What actually-profitable memecoin trader.topic: What actually-profitable memecoin traders do — mechanical rules with numbers (Solana / pump.fun, 2024–2026 sources)
What actually-profitable memecoin trader.executive_summary:
Three separate bodies of evidence were reachable: (1) shared screener presets from Axiom/BullX/GMGN/Solana-Tracker with real numeric thresholds, (2) two peer-reviewable arXiv datasets (MELT/MemeTrans, 41,470 launches; and a 655,770-token pump.fun census) that give hard base rates and feature importances, and (3) trader/vendor blog content that is mostly rule-shaped but unsourced.

The single most important quantitative finding for your bot: 60.26% of migrated memecoins drop below 20% of migration price within 20 minutes, and >73% drop below 40% within 20 minutes (MELT, n=41,470, Dec 2024–Mar 2025). This is a direct, hostile measurement of the popular "buy the post-graduation dip" trade — the dip is not a dip, it is the modal outcome. Your census's 1.000x median peak multiple is fully consistent with it.

Second most important: naive top-10 concentration systematically understates true concentration. After attributing bundled/co-funded wallets to single entities, median top-10 holding rises 24 percentage points for high-risk tokens vs only 6pp for low-risk ones. Your safety filter excludes pool addresses but if it does not cluster bundles (Jito bundle ID, co-purchase in same slot, common funding wallet), it is measuring the wrong quantity — and it is measuring it in exactly the way the adversary optimized against. Bundled accounts are 28.13% of holders and 36.50% of supply on average.

Third: the strongest published predictor of pump.fun graduation is liquidity accumulation speed (trades-to-vSOL ratio) — tokens reaching a given vSOL level in ≤10 trades graduate far more often than those needing 1,000+ — with non-bot trade share second (thresholds ≥0.3 and ≥0.7 both show step-ups). Median time-to-graduation is 4.4 minutes over ~457 trades. Note the tension with your design: your 60–300s wait is well-calibrated for filtering bot-only launches, but by 300s the median graduating token has already graduated, so your feed is structurally biased toward slower, more organic movers. That is probably correct for survival but you should confirm it is not also selecting out the winners.

The consensus mechanical numbers that recur across independent presets: top-10 ≤30% (strict) or ≤40% (permissive, early tokens); snipers ≤10–15%, hard reject >20%; dev/creator holding ≤10%; insiders ≤15–25%; bundle ≤20%; market-cap floor $9k–$20k; volume floor $2k (new) to $7–10k (post-graduation); holders ≥100 in hour one, ≥200–500 for concentration comfort; buy/sell ratio ≥2:1; token age windows 10–45 minutes.

Exit rules cluster tightly and independently on: stop at −30% to −50%, first rung at 1.5x–2x selling 25–50%, ladder 25% each at 2x/3x/5x/10x, and a time stop at 6–12 hours of no movement. Your 1.6x cost-recovery rung sits just below the modal 2x first rung — defensible given a 7.5% ever-2x base rate.

Explicitly unverifiable marketing: every "75% win rate" / "65–75% win rate" filter-preset claim, all "sub-50ms" and "70% same-block" execution claims, and the widely-repeated "healthy coin has ≥10% of market cap in liquidity" heuristic (no study underlies it). No genuine shared Dexscreener saved-filter URLs were locatable, and Photon's S1/S2/S3 "presets" are slippage/priority-fee profiles, not alpha filters — the marketing conflates the two. YouTube transcripts and X threads were not retrievable in full (transcript services returned only chapter metadata; the WebSearch budget was exhausted at 200 calls before Reddit/X could be worked directly), so trader-attributed rules below come from written secondary sources, not primary posts. I have marked those low confidence rather than inventing attributions.

findings.claim: 60.26% of migrated memecoins fall below 20% of their migration price within 20 minutes; >73% fall below 40%
findings.detail: MELT/MemeTrans dataset, 41,470 memecoin launches, 200M+ transactions parsed, Dec 1 2024 – Mar 1 2025. Risk labels are defined directly off this: min_price_ratio = (minimum price in the 20 min after migration) / (migration price). High-risk := min_price_ratio < 0.3; low-risk := min_price_ratio >= 0.7 AND manipulation score < 0.3. Resulting distribution: 84.13% high-risk, 11.34% medium, 4.53% low. Only 12.70% of tokens land in the 0.2–0.4 band. This is the hard measurement of the 'buy the post-migration dip' trade that every blog recommends: the dip is the modal outcome, not a discount.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do NOT implement a migration-dip limit-order ladder (the widely-recommended -20%/-40%/-60% ladder) as an unconditional entry. If you implement it at all, gate it: require the token to have already survived T+20min above 0.5x migration price before any bid rests. Equivalently, add a hard rule: no entry inside [migration_ts, migration_ts+20min]. Backtest by replaying your 924-launch census with a synthetic -20/-40/-60 ladder and measuring fill-to-recovery rate; expect it to be strictly worse than no-trade.

findings.claim: Bundled/coordinated wallets hold 36.50% of supply and are 28.13% of holders on average; attributing them lifts measured top-10 concentration by 24pp for high-risk tokens vs 6pp for low-risk
findings.detail: MELT breaks bundling into three detectable mechanisms with separate prevalence: fund-flow bundling (common funding wallet) 22.57% of holders / 28.22% of supply; Jito-bundle co-execution 10.39% of holders / 15.96% of supply; co-purchase (same-slot) 6.46% of holders / 9.16% of supply. High-risk tokens' first-10 buyers hold 17pp more supply than low-risk; first-20 buyers hold 19pp more. Transactions sharing a Jito bundle ID are described as strongly indicative of one entity. Pre-migration transaction composition: 73.5% normal buy/sell, 21.4% wash trades, 4.9% transfers. 98.7% of token-create events co-occur with a developer purchase.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your holder-concentration filter is measuring the wrong variable if it treats bundled wallets as independent. Add entity clustering before computing top-N: (a) group wallets sharing a Jito bundle ID in the launch window, (b) group wallets whose first SOL funding came from the same address within N blocks, (c) group wallets that bought in the same slot. Then apply the concentration threshold to clusters, not addresses. Also: the 21.4% wash-trade share means raw volume is inflated ~1.27x on average — deflate any volume-based score accordingly or you will systematically overrate manufactured activity.

findings.claim: Liquidity-accumulation speed (trades-to-vSOL ratio) is the strongest predictor of pump.fun graduation; non-bot trade share is second; 'top trader present' and 'prolific creator' are weak
findings.detail: arXiv study of the full pump.fun census: 655,770 tokens created, 243,123 unique creators, 2,600,790 distinct traders, Sep 1 – Oct 1 2025. Graduation rate 0.63% (4,338/655,770). Median time-to-graduation 4.4 minutes over a median ~457 trades. Graduation requires 85 SOL real reserves (115 SOL virtual+real, ~$69k mcap). Tokens reaching a given vSOL level in <=10 trades show substantially higher graduation probability than those needing 1,000+ trades. Non-bot fraction shows step-ups at >=0.3 and again at >=0.7. Creator identity is weak: best creator cohort graduated 8.4% (9/107), worst 2.3% (2/88) — a 3.7x spread, but both are small samples and both are far above base rate, i.e. 'has launched >=88 tokens' is itself the signal, not which prolific creator.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Add two features to your rule model with high weight: (1) sol_per_trade = liquidity added / trade count over the observation window — favor FEW LARGE buys over MANY SMALL ones, which is the opposite of the naive 'lots of transactions = interest' heuristic; (2) non_bot_trade_fraction, thresholded at 0.3 (min gate) and 0.7 (score bonus). Classify bot vs non-bot by inter-arrival regularity, identical trade sizes, and priority-fee signature. Testable directly against your 924-launch census: bucket by sol_per_trade quintile and compare peak-multiple distributions.

findings.claim: Shared Axiom Pulse preset, per-tab, with exact values
findings.detail: NEW PAIRS: snipers <=10%, dev holding <=10%, volume >=$500, market cap >=$5,000, protocols restricted to Pump and Bonk, at least one social = ON. FINAL STRETCH: age <=20 min, top-10 holders <=40%, snipers <=10%, dev holding <=10%, min pro traders >=3, volume >=$7,000, market cap >=$6,000. MIGRATED: top-10 holders <=40%, snipers <=10%, dev holding <=10%, min pro traders >=3, global fees paid >=1.5 SOL. The author explicitly states holders, bundle%, liquidity, insiders and bonding-curve % should be left BLANK and monitored manually rather than filtered — i.e. this preset deliberately does not filter on bundle, which per the MELT finding is the highest-signal variable available.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Use the 'global fees paid >= 1.5 SOL' idea — it is the cleverest number in the set. Cumulative protocol fees paid is a wash-trade-resistant proxy for real turnover because fees are burned, not recycled: a wash trader pays real SOL every round trip. Compute cumulative_fees_sol and require >=1.5 SOL post-migration. Also note 'min pro traders >= 3' is the recurring cross-platform structure: require >=3 wallets with an independently-verified profitable history, not 1.

findings.claim: Shared BullX NEO preset, per-tab, with exact values
findings.detail: NEW CREATIONS: market cap >=$9,000, transaction count last hour >=15, holders >=5, volume >=$2,000, token age <=10 min. ABOUT TO GRADUATE: market cap >=$15,000, token age <=25 min, bot users >=10, insider wallets <=25%. Auto-sell: stop-loss 30–40% below entry, take-profit 1.5x–2x, bribe ~0.01 SOL. Auto-buy: 0.5 SOL start, slippage 0.5–1% for low-volume / 10–15% for trending, priority fee 0.01 SOL. From a separate BullX tutorial: holders >=100 (of which >=25 should be genuine non-bot buyers), volume >=$10,000, age <=45 min (extend to 60–90 min only on strong momentum), >=200 users to avoid excessive volatility, market cap <$6,500 flagged as likely rugged, top-holder concentration example of 69% given as a red flag, stop-loss 30–40%, typical profit-taking at +90% to +100%.
findings.actionable_for_bot: The '>=25 of the 100 holders should be genuine regular buyers' rule is the useful one — it is a holder-quality gate, not a holder-count gate, and maps onto the non-bot-fraction finding from the arXiv census. Implement: genuine_holders = holders whose wallet has >=N prior unrelated token interactions and non-bot timing; require genuine_holders >= 25 AND genuine_holders/total_holders >= 0.25. The <=10 min / <=25 min / <=45 min age windows conflict with your 60–300s wait only at the short end; your window sits inside all of them.

findings.claim: Solana Tracker publishes explicit numeric rug-risk gates in a real API
findings.detail: Fields and thresholds: risk.snipers.totalPercentage — warn >15%, automated reject >20%. risk.bundlers.totalPercentage — warn >15%. risk.insiders.totalPercentage — warn >15%. risk.dev.percentage — creator's current position. risk.risks[] — mint authority, freeze authority, liquidity authority flags. Composite risk score on a 1–10 scale: below 3 'generally cleaner', 3–7 standard, above 7 'warrants extra scrutiny'. A boolean 'rugged' flag exists. The doc's own worked example gate is: score below 6 fails; snipers >20% fails; rugged status fails.
findings.actionable_for_bot: This is the most directly implementable third-party gate found and it is machine-readable. Adopt as a pre-filter alongside your own on-chain checks (do not replace them — vendor scores are opaque and can lag). Concrete gate: reject if snipers>20% OR bundlers>20% OR insiders>15% OR rugged==true. Test by scoring your 924-launch census retrospectively and checking whether the rejected set has a materially worse peak-multiple distribution than the accepted set; if the two distributions are indistinguishable, the vendor score adds nothing over your existing filter.

findings.claim: GMGN exposes a documented, parameterized screener API — these are the real filter primitives, not blog heuristics
findings.detail: Filter parameters (all min/max pairs): --min/max-holder-count; --min/max-top10-holder-rate (0–1); --min/max-top70-sniper-hold-rate (0–1); --min/max-bundler-rate (0–1, 'ratio of bot-bundled buys at launch'); --min/max-insider-rate (0–1); --min/max-entrapment-ratio (0–1); --min/max-dev-team-hold-rate (0–1); --min/max-volume (USD); --min/max-liquidity (USD); --min/max-marketcap (USD); --min/max-history-highest-marketcap (USD); --min/max-swaps; --min/max-buys-24h; --min/max-sells-24h; --min/max-gas-fee; --min/max-created (duration string, e.g. 30m/6h/7d); --min/max-smart-degen-count; --min/max-renowned-count. Solana default filter is 'renounced frozen'. Endpoints: GET /v1/market/token_kline (weight 2), GET /v1/market/rank (1), POST /v1/trenches (3), POST /v1/market/token_signal (3), POST /v1/market/hot_searches (3), GET /v1/market/search (1). Rate limit ~20/weight requests per second.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Two parameters here are not in your current filter set and are worth adding: history_highest_marketcap (lets you detect and reject 'already ran and round-tripped' tokens — a runner re-entry guard) and buys_24h/sells_24h as a directly computable buy/sell ratio. min-renowned-count / min-smart-degen-count give you a KOL-presence count you can use as a FADE signal rather than a confirm signal (see KOL finding). Rate limit ~6.7 rps on /v1/trenches is a real constraint for a scanner.

findings.claim: Top-10 holder limit: 30% is the strict consensus, 40% the permissive one, 20% the single-wallet red line
findings.detail: Multiple independent sources converge: GMGN practitioner guidance is 'total holdings of top 10 holders less than 30% of supply means dispersed holding, reducing single-whale manipulation risk'. Axiom guidance: 'Top 10 Holders' Max Ownership: 30% for healthier distribution... if the top 10 own over 30% it's likely a bundled coin or dev sniped their own coin' — while the shared per-tab preset uses the looser 40% because early tokens legitimately show high concentration. Single-wallet rules: >20% of supply in one wallet is a red flag; <10–15% is 'safer'. Creator/dev holding: >=30% signals dump risk; preset value is <=10%.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Recommend a tiered rule rather than one number, because the correct threshold is age-dependent: at age<10min accept top-10<=40%, at age 10–60min require <=30%, post-migration require <=25%. Critically — apply this to entity clusters, not raw addresses (see bundling finding), otherwise 30% measured naively is roughly 30%+24pp=54% true concentration on a high-risk token. Testable: on your census, compute peak-multiple distribution conditioned on cluster-adjusted top-10 in bands [0-20),[20-30),[30-40),[40+].

findings.claim: Market-cap entry bands actually cited: 7–15k ground floor, ~50k social-attention threshold, 69k graduation, 200k+ 'overhyped zone'
findings.detail: The 'trenches playbook' framing: Early 7–15k 'Ground Floor'; Mid ~50k 'Psychological Barrier' where a coin gains Crypto Twitter / Telegram attention and early buyers take partial profits; Late 200k+ 'Overhyped Zone' where entry is risky absent a strong catalyst. Graduation is fixed at 85 SOL real reserves / ~$69k. Separately cited operational floors: only trade under $500k mcap but with fast-growing volume; min $20k for 'early gems'; avoid sub-$10k for slippage/rug reasons; Axiom Pro cites a 9K+ minimum mcap filter. Also cited: >=$30,000 bonding-curve liquidity or >=$50,000 Raydium liquidity post-graduation as minimums.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Treat 50k as a regime boundary rather than an entry price. The claim that ~50k triggers social attention is testable on your census: measure holder-growth-rate and unique-buyer-rate as a function of mcap crossing 50k, and check for a discontinuity. If a real kink exists, entering at 30–45k with an exit rung placed just above 50k is a mechanically defensible setup; if no kink exists, the band is folklore and should be dropped. The 200k+ 'overhyped' claim is the weakest — it contradicts the fact that your 0.22%-ever-50x tail must pass through 200k+ by construction.

findings.claim: Exit ladders converge across independent sources on: stop −30% to −50%, first rung 1.5x–2x, 25% at each of 2x/3x/5x/10x
findings.detail: Collected variants: (a) sell 50% at 2x, stop −50%; (b) 25% at each of 2x, 3x, 5x, 10x with stop 30–50% below entry, plus a time-based exit 'if no movement in 6–12 hours, exit'; (c) sell 50% at 3x, 25% at 5x, let last 25% ride with a stop; (d) GMGN bot defaults: SL −30% to −40% standard (−25/−30 conservative, −45/−50 aggressive), TP 1.5–2x conservative / 2–3x standard / 3–5x aggressive; (e) BullX auto-sell: SL 30–40%, TP 1.5x–2x, typical profit-taking at +90–100%; (f) Axiom Pro in R-units: stop at −1R, staged exits of 30% at +2R and 30% at +4R; (g) a standalone 'fixed stop at −35% is a reasonable threshold'. Note (b) and (c) both leave a 25% moonbag with a stop — the 'never round-trip' rule expressed mechanically.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your 1.6x cost-recovery rung is below the modal 1.5–2x first rung, which is correct given your measured 7.5% ever-2x rate — at a 7.5% 2x rate, a first rung AT 2x fires on 7.5% of positions and is not a cost-recovery mechanism at all. Keep 1.6x. The one rule you may be missing is the TIME stop at 6–12h of no movement; with a 58-second average hold time market-wide, 6–12h is extremely generous and a 60–120 minute flat-time stop is more defensible. Test by measuring, on your census, P(peak multiple > 2x | no 1.3x touch within 60 min) — if that conditional is near zero, a 60-min flat stop is free.

findings.claim: KOL wallets are a fade signal, not a follow signal: they sell larger than they buy and cluster within 15 minutes
findings.detail: Dataset of 1.6M trades across 1,058 actively tracked KOL wallets. 30-day counts: 495,720 buys vs 337,124 sells (1.47:1). Average buy size 1.52 SOL, average sell size 2.24 SOL — i.e. they buy small across many names and exit large on the few that work; most buys go to zero and are never sold. Median win rate 57.1%, mean 63.3%; top performers hit 70–75% but trade only 3–5 tokens per day, and volume and accuracy are inversely correlated. Coordination: 9,404 cluster events in 30 days, average 5.1 KOLs per event, convergence window 15 minutes. Alert latency sub-2 seconds.
findings.actionable_for_bot: The mechanical KOL-fade setup: detect >=3 KOL/renowned wallets entering the same token within a 15-minute window (matches the observed 5.1-KOL cluster size and 15-min window), then treat that as a distribution event, not a confirmation. Two testable variants — (i) hard reject any token with a KOL cluster event, (ii) enter only AFTER the cluster's aggregate position has decreased by >50% from its peak. The 1.52-buy / 2.24-sell asymmetry is the concrete mechanism: their average exit is 1.47x their average entry in SOL terms, meaning the marginal follower is the exit liquidity. Also: 'win rate' here is per-trade and says nothing about PnL — a 57% win rate with 2.24/1.52 sizing is not evidence of edge for a copier who pays worse fills.

findings.claim: Deployer reputation is a genuinely large, exploitable signal: 34 'elite' deployers graduate at 71% vs a 1–2% base rate
findings.detail: Same KOL-tracking dataset: 10,600+ pump.fun deployers indexed. An 'elite tier' of 34 wallets is defined as having 5+ launches AND a 40%+ graduation rate; that tier's realized graduation rate is 71% (~7 of 10 tokens bond) against an overall pump.fun graduation rate quoted as 1–2% (the arXiv census measures 0.63% for Sep 2025). That is a 35–110x lift. Caveat: the elite tier is selected on the same statistic being reported, so it is partly survivorship — a forward-tested version would need to freeze the tier on data up to time T and measure T+1 performance.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Highest-value-per-unit-effort addition to your scorer. You already track creator mint-count as a NEGATIVE (serial minters). Split it: maintain a per-deployer rolling record of (launches, graduations, median peak multiple) and score deployers with >=5 prior launches on their realized graduation rate, not on launch count alone. Test properly with a walk-forward split to kill the selection bias: rank deployers on months 1–2, measure month 3. If the month-3 lift survives at even 5–10x, this dominates every screener threshold in this report.

findings.claim: Bot activity stabilizes after the first 5–10 minutes — this is the stated rationale for delayed entry and it corroborates your 60–300s wait
findings.detail: Multiple sources independently place the bot-noise decay at 5–10 minutes: 'consistent buying in the first 5–10 minutes' is cited as the favorable early-entry volume indicator, and 'after the first 5–10 minutes' is when bot activity is said to stabilize. Separately, 'most pumps or rugs occur within about four hours' and 'the majority of 2x+ moves happen within the first few hours of the token hitting a usable liquidity threshold'. Independently, 66% of coins lose >90% of available liquidity within the first 24 hours.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your 60–300s window sits at the aggressive edge of the cited 5–10 min (300–600s) stabilization band. Worth an A/B: run the existing 60–300s arm against a 300–600s arm on live paper and compare fill quality and 20-minute survival. The counter-consideration is real and quantified elsewhere in this report: median time-to-graduation is 4.4 min, so waiting to 600s means the fastest-bonding cohort is entirely gone. Frame the choice explicitly as 'trade the slow organic tail' (your current design) vs 'trade the fast cohort' — do not try to do both with one window.

findings.claim: Average hold time on Solana memecoins collapsed to 58 seconds in 2026, from ~100 seconds in 2025 and ~24 hours in 2024
findings.detail: Reported off Dune Analytics. Cited range across datasets is 44–62 seconds for 2026. The article acknowledges that much of the underlying volume is automated (snipers, copy-traders, high-frequency setups) but does not quantify the bot share, and provides no percentile distribution — only the single average per year. The 24h-to-58s collapse over two years is the headline; the absence of a distribution means the mean is likely dragged down hard by bot round-trips and should not be read as 'the typical human holds 58 seconds'.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Sets the timescale for your dump detector and your trail. If the population round-trip is ~1 minute, a Shewhart baseline window measured in trades (the arXiv paper uses 30–200 trades, k=4 sigma — identical to your 4-sigma choice) is more robust than one measured in wall-clock seconds, because trade arrival rate varies by two orders of magnitude across tokens. Recommend: if your dump detector currently uses a time-based baseline, switch to a trade-count baseline of 30–200 trades to match the published parameterization you already mirror.

findings.claim: Reported trader profitability is 94% losing over 90 days but 73.28% profitable in a single month — these measure different things and are routinely conflated
findings.detail: Two figures circulate. (1) Roughly 94% of Solana memecoin traders lose money over a 90-day window; only 6.25% of 304,161 active wallets were profitable over the trailing 90 days. (2) CoinGecko-sourced monthly pump.fun data: share of profitable traders fell below 50% every month from June 2024 through December 2025, bottoming at 30.08% in June 2025, then rose from 50.08% in January 2026 to 73.28% by April 2026. Distribution among profitable wallets is tiny: ~2.05M wallets (65.1%) earned $1–$500; 87,000 (2.8%) earned $500–$1,000; 169,000 (5.4%) earned above $1,000. A commonly quoted planning assumption is that 70–85% of memecoin trades lose money.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do not use the 73.28% monthly figure to justify loosening risk. A wallet counts as 'profitable this month' on any positive realized PnL, including +$3; the $1–$500 bucket being 65.1% of winners shows the win distribution is dominated by trivial amounts, while the 90-day figure captures the fee-and-slippage drag that kills those wallets over time. The right planning prior for your sizing is the 70–85% per-trade loss rate, which is consistent with your own measured 7.5% ever-2x. Your fractional-Kelly-capped-at-2%-of-pool-depth sizing is the correct response to this distribution; nothing here argues for increasing it.

findings.claim: Buy/sell ratio entry confirmation at >=2:1, with accelerating volume
findings.detail: Cited as an entry-confirmation signal: 'traders look for buy/sell ratios of at least 2:1 and accelerating volume'. For calibration, the aggregate KOL-wallet population runs at 1.47:1 buys:sells over 30 days, so 2:1 on a single token is meaningfully above the ambient rate. GMGN exposes buys_24h and sells_24h as first-class filter parameters, making this directly computable. No source found provides a 5-minute or 1-hour buy/sell ratio threshold specifically; the 2:1 figure is stated without a window.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Implement as a windowed ratio, since the source omits the window: compute buy_count/sell_count over both 5-min and 60-min windows and require >=2.0 on the 5-min AND >=1.5 on the 60-min (the second condition rejects a single burst). Better still, use unique-buyer/unique-seller counts rather than transaction counts, which is wash-trade resistant given the measured 21.4% wash-trade share. Testable on your census by bucketing 5-min buy/sell ratio at entry time against realized peak multiple.

findings.claim: The 'healthy coin has >=10% of market cap in the liquidity pool' rule is universally repeated and has no identifiable source study
findings.detail: Stated as a mechanical filter: 'a healthy meme coin usually has at least 10 percent of its market cap in the liquidity pool... traders use a liquidity-to-market-cap ratio threshold and toss anything below 10%'. A separate variant garbles it into 'volume at least 10% of cap'. Related but distinct and better-grounded: sector-level Trading-Volume-to-Market-Cap (TV-MC) for Solana memecoins measured at 0.26 ($3.5B volume / $13.4B mcap), with the claim that TV-MC of 0.2–0.5 indicates 'a maturing market without extreme speculation' — that interpretive band is itself unsourced.
findings.actionable_for_bot: The 10% liquidity/mcap ratio is worth implementing anyway, but for a mechanical reason the folklore does not state: it directly bounds your slippage, and you already size at 2% of pool depth. At L/MC = 10%, a 2%-of-pool position is 0.2% of mcap; at L/MC = 3% it is 0.06% of mcap — so the ratio is really a position-capacity constraint, not a quality signal. Reframe it that way and set the floor from your minimum viable position size, not from the folklore number. Flag the 'maturing market' TV-MC interpretation as unverifiable narrative.

findings.claim: Holder-count thresholds cited: >=100 in the first hour, >=200 users, >=500 for 'materially reduced concentration risk'
findings.detail: Three distinct numbers appear. (1) '100+ holders in the first hour' paired with 'volume flipping market cap (high turnover = strong interest)' and 'market cap under $500K'. (2) '>=200 users recommended to avoid excessive volatility'. (3) '500+ holders — community concentration risk drops materially above this threshold'. None of the three is accompanied by supporting data, and the 500 figure in particular is asserted without any concentration measurement. Countervailing: the BullX tutorial's more careful framing requires >=100 holders of which >=25 are genuine non-bot buyers, which is a quality-adjusted version of the same gate.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Prefer the holder-GROWTH-RATE form over the level form, because level is trivially manufactured by a bundler for a few cents in rent: track unique_new_buyers_per_minute over your 60–300s observation window and require a positive second derivative (acceleration), plus the absolute gate of >=25 genuine holders. Test the level thresholds directly on your census — bucket at 100/200/500 holders at T+300s and compare peak-multiple distributions. My prior is that raw holder count will show near-zero discriminative power once bundle clusters are collapsed, and that is a cheap, decisive experiment to run.

findings.claim: Copy-trading source-wallet selection criteria: >60% win rate over 30+ trades, >7-day history, 5–7 wallets max, mirror at 10–20% of source size
findings.detail: GMGN bot guidance. Full set: wallet count 5–7 max (range 3–10 across risk profiles), minimum >60% win rate over 30+ trades, >7-day history requirement, mirror size 10–20% of source (5–10% conservative, 20–30% aggressive). Position sizing 0.1–0.5 SOL per trade, max 2–5% of trading wallet. Note the sample-size problem: 30 trades at a true 50% win rate produces an observed win rate above 60% about 10% of the time by chance, and there are hundreds of thousands of candidate wallets — so a >60%-over-30-trades screen applied across the population selects almost entirely noise.
findings.actionable_for_bot: If you ever add copy-trading, the 30-trade minimum is far too low. Require >=200 trades and evaluate on realized SOL PnL net of fees, not win rate — the KOL data (1.52 SOL average buy, 2.24 SOL average sell, 57.1% median win rate) shows win rate and profitability are close to decoupled in this market. Also enforce a walk-forward split: rank wallets on a training period, measure on a disjoint later period. Report the lift; if it is under 1.5x, do not build it.

findings.claim: Execution parameter consensus: slippage 10–15% for new launches, priority fee 0.01–0.03 SOL, Jito bribe 0.001–0.03 SOL, MEV protection on for launches
findings.detail: Two independent platforms give near-identical numbers. GMGN: slippage 10–15% standard on new pump.fun launches, 15–20% on hot launches, 5–8% established; priority fee 0.01–0.03 SOL standard, 0.05–0.1 SOL on competitive launches; MEV modes Off/Reduced/Secure with Secure recommended for launches. Axiom: slippage conservative 0.5–2%, balanced 5–10%, aggressive 15–30%; priority fee default 0.001 SOL, balanced 0.002–0.03, aggressive 0.03–0.1; bribe default 0.001 SOL, 0.01 SOL for exit orders, up to 0.1 on competitive blocks. BullX: slippage 0.5–1% low-volume, 10–15% trending; priority fee 0.01 SOL; bribe ~0.01 SOL. Photon's S1/S2/S3 'presets' are only slippage/priority-fee/Jito-bribe profiles — they contain no screening logic despite being marketed as trading presets.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Note the asymmetry every source implies but none states: bribe on EXIT (0.01 SOL cited by Axiom) matters more than on entry, because your exit competes with the dump. Given your 4-sigma dump detector, budget a materially higher priority fee and Jito tip on detector-triggered exits than on scale-out rungs — the detector firing means you are racing. Model the fee as part of the exit cost in your Kelly sizing: at 0.01–0.1 SOL per exit across a laddered scale-out with 4+ rungs, fees are a non-trivial drag on small positions and argue for fewer, larger rungs at your size.

findings.claim: Position sizing consensus: 0.5–2% of active capital per bet, 5–15% of portfolio in the memecoin sleeve
findings.detail: Barbell structure recurring across sources: majority of capital in cash or SOL, 5–15% of the active trading account allocated to memecoins, split across many positions rather than concentrated, each individual bet at 0.5–2% of the active account. Separate statements: 'never risk more than 0.5–1% of trading capital on a single pump.fun trade' with the explicit arithmetic 'with 10 trades at 1% each and an 80% loss rate, you are down 8% on the bad streak'; 'no single position should exceed 5–10% of total trading capital'; individual positions of 0.1–0.3 SOL; Axiom Pro 'position sizes 1–2% of portfolio per trade'; GMGN '0.1–0.5 SOL per trade, max 2–5% of trading wallet'. Practical minimum starting capital cited as $200–500.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your fractional-Kelly sizing capped at 2% of pool depth is a market-impact constraint; these numbers are a bankroll constraint. You need BOTH, and the binding one should be min(kelly_fraction * bankroll, 0.02 * pool_depth, 0.02 * bankroll). The 0.5–2%-of-bankroll cap is the one that survives a model error in your Kelly estimate — given a 7.5% ever-2x base rate, a mis-estimated edge makes full Kelly catastrophic, and the folk cap at 2% is roughly what quarter-Kelly on these base rates produces anyway. Worth checking that your fractional-Kelly output is not routinely exceeding 2% of bankroll.

findings.claim: The post-graduation limit-order ladder is specified as -20% / -40% / -60% below graduation price with equal SOL per tier
findings.detail: The concrete form of the 'buy the migration dip' trade: three buy orders at -20%, -40% and -60% below graduation price, equal SOL allocation at each tier, on the rationale that 'many pump.fun tokens retrace 40–90% after initial hype fades' and '40–70% shortly after launch due to bot pressure and fading momentum'. The stated logic is to avoid timing the bottom by spreading entries. Set directly against the MELT measurement: 60.26% of migrated tokens go below 20% of migration price (i.e. -80%) within 20 minutes, meaning all three ladder tiers fill on the majority of tokens and the average fill is deep inside a continuing collapse.
findings.actionable_for_bot: This is the clearest case in the report where a popular named setup is contradicted by data. The ladder's fill rate is near 100% on the losers and low on the winners — textbook adverse selection. If you want the migration trade, invert it: place NO resting bids, wait the full 20 minutes, and only then buy tokens whose min_price_ratio over that window stayed >=0.5 (the low-risk cohort is 4.53% of launches, which is a small but genuinely differentiated population). Test by replaying both variants over your census and comparing realized PnL and fill-conditional peak multiple.

findings.claim: Consolidation-breakout and dip-entry setups are stated with real numbers but on timeframes irrelevant to sub-hour memecoins
findings.detail: The 'first green candle after consolidation' setup as actually specified: mark support/resistance of the consolidation zone, wait for a volume spike (breakouts on low volume are fakeouts), and buy when price closes above resistance on the 4-HOUR OR DAILY timeframe with volume at 2x the average. The dip-entry variant: wait for volume to dry up (sellers exhausted), take a bullish engulfing candle as the buy signal, stop at -20%. The 2x-average-volume breakout confirmation and the -20% stop are the transferable numbers; the 4h/daily timeframe is not, given a 58-second average hold time and a 4.4-minute median time-to-graduation.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Rescale the timeframe by roughly the ratio of hold times (4h daily-chart logic maps to something like 1–5 minute bars here) and keep only the two numeric components: require breakout-bar volume >= 2.0x the trailing average bar volume, and use a -20% stop on breakout entries specifically (tighter than your general hard stop, justified because a failed breakout invalidates immediately). Testable: define consolidation as a k-bar range compression on 1-min bars, and measure P(peak > 2x | breakout with vol>=2x avg) against the 7.5% unconditional base rate. If it does not clear ~15%, discard the setup.

findings.claim: Behavioral circuit-breakers are stated as absolute rules with no numeric tolerance — and these are the only rules stated without hedging anywhere in the corpus
findings.detail: Two hard rules: 'If you ever freeze on a stop loss, end the session immediately' and 'If you re-enter the same token after a loss on it, the session ends immediately — a re-entry after a loss means your psychology is now driving decisions.' The same source gives exactly one number in the entire piece: '-35% is a reasonable threshold' for a fixed stop loss. Everything else in it is deliberately non-numeric, on the stated view that discipline structure matters more than parameter values.
findings.actionable_for_bot: The re-entry ban translates directly into a bot rule and is worth implementing because it also has a market-structure justification, not just a psychological one: re-entering a token you stopped out of means buying into a population that has already demonstrated distribution. Implement a per-mint cooldown — after a stop-out or dump-detector exit on mint M, blacklist M permanently (or for >=24h). This is the mechanical form of 'runner re-entry' risk control, and it is cheap and testable: measure realized PnL on all second-entries in your census versus first-entries.

findings.claim: Every win-rate claim attached to a filter preset is marketing and none carries a methodology
findings.detail: Specific unverifiable claims encountered: 'BEST BullX Neo Filters & Settings (75% WINRATE)' as a page title, softened in the body to 'intermediate traders can achieve 65-75% win rate' with the disclaimer that 'meme coin trading is still high-risk'. No sample size, no time period, no trade log, no definition of 'win'. Similarly unverifiable execution claims: 'sub-50ms execution latency via private nodes' and 'approximately 70% same-block execution rate' for copy trading — both vendor performance assertions with no measurement methodology. Also flagged: Photon's three 'presets' are marketed as trading presets but contain only slippage, priority fee and Jito bribe values, with zero screening logic.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Assign zero weight to any preset because of its advertised win rate; weight it only by whether the individual thresholds survive your own census backtest. Note the structural incentive: these platforms earn per-trade fees (BullX cited at ~0.9%), so their published presets are optimized for trade frequency, not for trader PnL. Concretely, that predicts their thresholds are systematically too LOOSE — which matches what we see (BullX 'New Creations' accepts holders>=5 and age<=10min, which admits essentially every launch). Tighten every borrowed threshold before testing it.

findings.claim: Two-thirds of memecoins lose >90% of liquidity within 24 hours, and pump.fun graduation is ~0.63–1%
findings.detail: Analysis of 493,203 Raydium pools / 474,161 unique tokens as of Nov 25 2024: 'nearly two out of three coins have been slaughtered within the first 24 hours with >90% of available liquidity evaporated'. Approximately 1 in 100 tokens reach the $69k graduation threshold; pump.fun accounted for 71.9% of memecoin launches. Market cap distribution clusters primarily in the $100–$10,000 band, with a secondary concentration at $5,000–$15,000 for graduates. The arXiv census measures the graduation rate more precisely at 0.63% (4,338 of 655,770) for September 2025.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Confirms your census's 1.000x median peak multiple from an independent dataset and an independent year — good cross-validation that your measurement is unbiased rather than an artifact of your discovery feed. Practical use: the >90%-liquidity-evaporation-in-24h rate is the correct denominator for your time stop. If two-thirds of tokens are structurally dead within 24h, any position held past ~4h (the cited window for most pumps and rugs) is holding through the period when liquidity leaves, which means your exit slippage assumption degrades over the holding period and should be modeled as time-varying, not constant.

findings.claim: No genuine shared Dexscreener saved-filter configurations were locatable, and no primary X threads or YouTube transcripts could be retrieved
findings.detail: Coverage gaps, stated explicitly rather than filled with invention. (1) Dexscreener: no shared saved-preset URLs or exported filter configs with numeric values were found in reachable sources. (2) X/Twitter: the WebSearch budget (200 calls, session cap) was exhausted before named-trader threads could be worked directly; the one X post surfaced was commentary on KOL coordination, not a rules thread. (3) YouTube: transcript aggregators (videohighlight.com) returned only chapter titles and timestamps, not transcript bodies, for all five candidate videos including 'BEST Axiom Setup to Trade Memecoins (FILTERS+SETTINGS+WALLETS)'. (4) Reddit: reddit.com is blocked to this user agent, so r/solana, r/CryptoCurrency, r/memecoins and r/pumpfun could not be searched at all. (5) Several sources returned 403 to automated fetching (Medium articles, gate.com, beincrypto, coinlaw, dextools).
findings.actionable_for_bot: Treat the trader-attributed rules in this report as secondary-source paraphrase, not as verified quotes from named traders. If primary-source attribution matters for your decisions, the retrievable paths are: a browser session with transcript extraction for the five YouTube video IDs (4gEYqkntWEI, 7WDI_Y99_kw, QnxLgB5RRU4, Ai2Ab6TT21Y, z3TZ_lWtJcU), and Reddit via its public JSON API from a non-blocked agent. The arXiv datasets (MELT and the pump.fun census) are the only primary quantitative sources here and should carry the weight in any parameter decision.

The bundler percentage is the single field most worth consuming, since computing it yourself requires Jito bundle-ID indexing.

concrete_apis.name: MELT / MemeTrans dataset
concrete_apis.what_it_gives: 41,470 memecoin launches, 200M+ transactions, 22,668,222 transactions with Jito bundle IDs, 1,916,363 pre-migration and 6,538,577 post-migration unique accounts, Dec 2024-Mar 2025. 122 engineered features across context, trading activity, holding concentration and time-series dynamics, with bundle-level entity attribution. Directly usable as an out-of-sample validation set for your safety filter and scorer, and as a labeled training set (min_price_ratio<0.3 = high risk).

concrete_apis.name: pump.fun full-census study
concrete_apis.what_it_gives: 655,770 tokens, 243,123 creators, 2,600,790 traders, Sep 1-Oct 1 2025. Establishes the 0.63% graduation rate, 4.4-minute median time-to-graduation, ~457 median trades to graduate, trades-to-vSOL as the dominant predictor, and non-bot fraction thresholds at 0.3 and 0.7. Also independently uses a Shewhart k=4 dump detector with a 30-200 trade baseline window, i.e. the same parameterization your bot already uses.

concrete_apis.name: Bitquery pump.fun to PumpSwap migration API
concrete_apis.what_it_gives: Migration event tracking, which is the trigger you need to timestamp t=0 for the 20-minute post-migration survival gate recommended in the findings. Not fetched in full in this session — verify endpoint shape and pricing before integrating.

numeric_parameters.value: 20 minutes; then require min_price_ratio >= 0.5 over that window
numeric_parameters.rationale: 60.26% of migrated tokens go below 0.2x migration price within 20 min and >73% below 0.4x (MELT, n=41,470). Any resting bid inside this window is adversely selected. The surviving cohort (min_price_ratio>=0.7) is 4.53% of launches and is genuinely differentiated.

numeric_parameters.value: <=40% at age<10min, <=30% at age 10-60min, <=25% post-migration — applied to ENTITY CLUSTERS not addresses
numeric_parameters.rationale: 30% is the strict cross-platform consensus and 40% the permissive one. Cluster adjustment is mandatory: bundle attribution raises median top-10 by 24pp on high-risk tokens vs 6pp on low-risk, so 30% naive is ~54% true on a bad token.

numeric_parameters.value: reject if bundled/coordinated supply > 20%
numeric_parameters.rationale: Population mean is 36.50% of supply across 28.13% of holders. Axiom guidance suggests 20% max 'to clear out obvious bad coins'. Bundle statistics were one of the two highest-importance feature groups in the MELT Random Forest.

numeric_parameters.value: warn >10%, hard reject >20%
numeric_parameters.rationale: Axiom presets use <=10% across all three tabs; Solana Tracker warns at >15% and its worked example gate rejects at >20%. Two independent sources converge on the 20% reject line.
Solana Tracker warns >15%; BullX preset uses <=25% which is looser than the vendor's own risk API and reflects fee-maximizing incentives. Take the tighter of the two.

Axiom presets use <=10% on all three tabs. Independent red-flag lines cited at >20% for any single wallet and >=30% for creator specifically; 10% is the operational preset value and the tightest defensible.

numeric_parameters.value: gate at >=0.30, score bonus at >=0.70
numeric_parameters.rationale: Both thresholds show distinct step-ups in graduation probability in the 655,770-token census. Second-strongest published predictor after liquidity accumulation speed.

numeric_parameters.value: favor high; tokens reaching a given vSOL in <=10 trades vastly outperform those needing 1,000+
numeric_parameters.rationale: Strongest single predictor of graduation in the full pump.fun census. Inverts the naive 'high transaction count = interest' heuristic, which mostly measures bots and wash trades.

numeric_parameters.value: multiply raw volume by ~0.79
numeric_parameters.rationale: Pre-migration transaction composition measured at 73.5% normal / 21.4% wash / 4.9% transfers. Any volume-based score is inflated ~1.27x on average if unadjusted, and inflated far more on the manipulated tail.

numeric_parameters.value: >=2.0 on 5-min window AND >=1.5 on 60-min window, using UNIQUE buyers/sellers
numeric_parameters.rationale: 2:1 is the cited entry-confirmation figure (window unspecified in source). Ambient KOL-population rate is 1.47:1, so 2:1 is a real excess. Unique-wallet counting rather than transaction counting defeats the 21.4% wash share.

numeric_parameters.value: >=25 non-bot holders AND genuine/total >= 0.25
numeric_parameters.rationale: The quality-adjusted version of the '>=100 holders' folklore, from the BullX tutorial. Raw holder count is trivially manufactured; the >=25-genuine form is the only holder gate in the corpus that resists bundling.

numeric_parameters.value: >=1.5 SOL post-migration
numeric_parameters.rationale: From the shared Axiom Migrated preset. Best wash-trade-resistant turnover proxy found: fees are burned rather than recycled, so a wash trader pays real SOL every round trip. Cheapest high-signal filter in the report.

numeric_parameters.value: >=10%, but treated as a position-capacity constraint
numeric_parameters.rationale: The 10% figure is unsourced folklore, but at your 2%-of-pool sizing it mechanically bounds position size as a fraction of mcap (0.2% of mcap at L/MC=10%, 0.06% at L/MC=3%). Derive the real floor from your minimum viable position, not from the folklore.

numeric_parameters.value: >=$30k bonding-curve, >=$50k post-graduation Raydium/PumpSwap
numeric_parameters.rationale: Cited operational minimums; consistent with the $69k graduation mcap and with the need for exit depth given time-varying slippage.
Independently converged on by GMGN defaults (-30 to -40), BullX auto-sell (30-40%), the altrady ladder (30-50%) and a standalone '-35% is reasonable'. Four independent sources in a tight band.

numeric_parameters.value: 1.6x (keep yours; do not move to 2.0x)
numeric_parameters.rationale: Modal published first rung is 1.5x-2.0x, but at your measured 7.5% ever-2x rate a rung placed AT 2x fires on 7.5% of positions and provides no cost recovery. 1.6x sits inside the published band and above your 1.000x median.

numeric_parameters.value: 25% at each of 2x / 3x / 5x / 10x after the cost-recovery rung, moonbag under trail
numeric_parameters.rationale: Most commonly stated full ladder. Variant (50% at 3x, 25% at 5x, 25% trailing) is the same shape. Both preserve a trailed remainder, which is the mechanical form of 'never round-trip a 5x'.

numeric_parameters.value: 60-120 minutes flat (published figure is 6-12 hours — far too loose)
numeric_parameters.rationale: Published rule is 'no movement in 6-12 hours, exit'. Against a 58-second average hold time, a 4.4-minute median time-to-graduation and 'most pumps or rugs within ~4 hours', 6-12h is an order of magnitude too generous. Validate with P(peak>2x | no 1.3x touch within 60min) on your census.

numeric_parameters.value: k=4 sigma, baseline window 30-200 TRADES (not seconds)
numeric_parameters.rationale: Exactly the parameterization independently used in the 655,770-token census. Trade-count baselines are robust to the two-orders-of-magnitude variation in trade arrival rate across tokens; wall-clock baselines are not.

numeric_parameters.value: min(fractional_kelly * bankroll, 2% of pool depth, 2% of bankroll)
numeric_parameters.rationale: Your 2%-of-pool cap is a market-impact constraint; the folk consensus of 0.5-2% per bet is a bankroll constraint. Both must bind. At a 7.5% ever-2x base rate, an over-estimated edge makes full Kelly ruinous, and 2% of bankroll is roughly quarter-Kelly on these rates.

numeric_parameters.value: >=3 KOL/renowned wallets entering within 15 minutes = distribution event
numeric_parameters.rationale: Measured coordination: 9,404 cluster events in 30 days, mean 5.1 KOLs per event, 15-minute convergence window. Average KOL sell (2.24 SOL) is 1.47x average KOL buy (1.52 SOL) — the follower is the exit liquidity.

numeric_parameters.value: score deployers with >=5 prior launches by realized graduation rate; elite tier graduates at 71% vs 0.63% base
numeric_parameters.rationale: Largest lift of any signal found (35-110x). Must be walk-forward validated because the published elite tier was selected on the statistic being reported.

numeric_parameters.value: permanent per-mint blacklist after any stop-out or detector exit (minimum 24h)
numeric_parameters.rationale: Stated as an absolute discipline rule, but has an independent market-structure justification: a token that stopped you out has demonstrated active distribution.

numeric_parameters.value: 0.01-0.1 SOL on detector-triggered exits; 0.001-0.01 SOL on scheduled rungs
numeric_parameters.rationale: Axiom cites 0.01 SOL specifically for exit orders and up to 0.1 on competitive blocks. A firing dump detector means you are racing informed sellers, so exit fees should be state-dependent, not constant.

numeric_parameters.value: >=2.0x trailing average bar volume
numeric_parameters.rationale: The one transferable number from the consolidation-breakout setup ('breakouts on low volume are fakeouts'). Timeframe in the source is 4h/daily and must be rescaled to 1-5 minute bars for this market.

traps_and_failure_modes: THE BIG ONE: the 'buy the post-migration dip' trade is contradicted by the best available data. 60.26% of migrated tokens go below 0.2x migration price within 20 minutes. The specific -20%/-40%/-60% resting ladder every guide recommends fills all three tiers on the majority of tokens and is pure adverse selection: near-100% fill on losers, low fill on winners. Do not implement it as specified.

Naive top-10 holder concentration is the wrong measurement and is adversarially optimized against. Bundle attribution adds 24pp to high-risk tokens' top-10 but only 6pp to low-risk ones — so an unclustered filter is close to non-discriminating on exactly the population you are trying to reject. If your bot excludes pool addresses but not bundle clusters, its flagship safety filter is substantially cosmetic.

Raw volume is inflated ~1.27x on average by wash trading (21.4% of pre-migration transactions) and much more on manipulated tokens. Any volume floor, volume/mcap ratio, or volume-acceleration feature rewards manufactured activity unless deflated or replaced with a wash-resistant proxy (cumulative burned fees, unique buyer counts).

Transaction count is an anti-signal, not a signal. The strongest published graduation predictor is FEW LARGE trades (trades-to-vSOL), yet the borrowed presets gate on 'transaction count last hour >= 15' and 'bot users >= 10', which select for the opposite. Do not import high-txn-count gates without inverting the intuition.

Platform-published presets are fee-maximizing, not PnL-maximizing. BullX charges ~0.9% per trade; its 'New Creations' preset accepts holders>=5, age<=10min, mcap>=$9k — which admits essentially every launch. Every borrowed threshold should be assumed too loose and tightened before testing.

Every advertised win rate in this corpus is unfalsifiable marketing: '75% WINRATE' filter presets, '65-75% for intermediate traders', 'sub-50ms private node execution', '70% same-block copy execution'. None carries a sample size, period, trade log, or definition of a win. Assign zero weight.

The 73.28%-profitable-in-April-2026 figure will be misused to justify loosening risk. It counts any wallet with positive realized monthly PnL including +$3 (65.1% of winners are in the $1-500 bucket), while the 94%-lose-over-90-days figure captures the fee and slippage drag that actually kills wallets. Use the 70-85% per-trade loss rate as the planning prior.

Your 60-300s observation window structurally excludes the fastest-bonding cohort: median time-to-graduation is 4.4 minutes. You are, by construction, trading the slow organic tail. That is likely the right choice, but it must be a deliberate one — verify the winners are not concentrated in the cohort your window discards.

'>60% win rate over 30 trades' as a copy-trade filter is statistically meaningless. At a true 50% rate, 30 trades clears 60% about 10% of the time by chance; screened across hundreds of thousands of wallets it selects pure noise. Require >=200 trades, evaluate on net SOL PnL not win rate, and use a walk-forward split.

Win rate and profitability are close to decoupled here. KOL wallets show a 57.1% median win rate while buying at 1.52 SOL average and selling at 2.24 SOL average — the win-rate statistic tells you nothing about whether following them is profitable, and a copier gets strictly worse fills.

The elite-deployer 71% graduation rate is selected on the same statistic it reports. The signal is probably real and is the largest lift in this report, but the effect size will shrink substantially under walk-forward validation. Do not size on the 71% figure.

Holder-count thresholds (100 / 200 / 500) are stated everywhere and sourced nowhere, and holder count is among the cheapest metrics for an adversary to manufacture. Expect near-zero discriminative power once bundle clusters are collapsed; test before implementing.

The '>=10% of market cap in liquidity' rule is universally repeated folklore with no underlying study. It is still worth implementing, but as a position-capacity constraint derived from your own sizing — not as a quality signal.

Exit slippage is time-varying, not constant. Two-thirds of tokens lose >90% of liquidity within 24 hours, so a slippage assumption calibrated at entry is badly wrong for a position held hours. Model exit depth as decaying.

Wall-clock baselines break the dump detector. Trade arrival rates vary by two orders of magnitude across tokens; the published k=4 Shewhart parameterization uses a 30-200 TRADE baseline for exactly this reason.

Laddered scale-outs have a fee floor. At 0.01-0.1 SOL priority fee plus bribe per exit across 4+ rungs, small positions can lose a meaningful fraction of edge to exit costs alone — which argues for fewer, larger rungs at small size.
Photon's S1/S2/S3 'presets' are slippage and priority-fee profiles containing no screening logic whatsoever, but are marketed and widely cited as trading presets. Do not expect alpha from them.

Coverage gap, stated plainly: Reddit is inaccessible to this agent, YouTube transcript services returned only chapter metadata, the 200-call WebSearch budget was exhausted before X threads could be worked, and several sources (Medium, gate.com, beincrypto, coinlaw, dextools) returned 403. Trader-attributed rules here are secondary-source paraphrase. Only the two arXiv datasets are primary quantitative sources and only they should carry weight in parameter decisions.
